# Spark Agent full product summary

Spark Agent is an open-source, local-first AI Agent workbench. It is built as an Electron desktop application with a React 19 renderer, typed IPC, an Agent Runtime package, local SQLite repositories, workspace files, asset storage, and system credential storage.

## What Spark Agent does
Spark Agent helps users develop code, debug failures, review generated patches, isolate sessions in Git worktrees, coordinate multiple agents, configure models and tools, and organize multimedia or film production workflows. It also supports writing documentation, drafting plans and PRDs, preparing presentation outlines, generating web content, and processing local files.

## Development workbench
The coding surface combines side chat, built-in terminal, file context, Git Review, HunkDiff, checkpoints, debug mode, browser automation, task status, and optional remote connections. The goal is to make Agent edits observable and reversible instead of hiding them behind a chat transcript.

## Runtime governance
The runtime includes Claude Agent SDK and Codex execution paths, MCP client/server integration, provider configuration, session management, permissions, usage ledger, rules, hooks, memory services, team dispatch, media task routing, and audit events.

## Team Agent mode
Team mode lets a Host Agent dispatch tasks to member agents. Each member can have its own model, tools, Skills, MCP servers, context, budget, timeout, and event stream. The UI presents the process as a group workflow so users can inspect delegation and results.

## Infinite canvas
The infinite canvas is the creative hub. It can organize scripts, characters, scenes, props, shots, storyboards, prompts, generation tasks, and produced assets in one visual workspace. It includes Film Asset Center, Shot Director, Prompt Library, timeline, storyboard grid, AI panel, and operation panel concepts.

## FAQ
Q: Is Spark Agent local-first? A: Yes, project data and runtime state are designed around local desktop storage.
Q: Is Spark Agent only for developers? A: No, developers can use the coding loop, while product, operations, education, consulting, and film teams can use canvas, assets, and media workflows.
Q: Can it create film storyboards? A: It includes an infinite-canvas film workflow with script breakdown, shot planning, storyboard grids, film assets, timelines, and generation-task organization.
Q: Which models are supported? A: Text paths include Claude Agent SDK and Codex. Model, image, video, and audio capabilities depend on configured providers and manifests.
Q: How does it reduce Agent risk? A: It exposes worktrees, checkpoints, Git Review, HunkDiff, permission approval, usage ledger, and audit events.
